"When you look at the airline business, lending against aircraft is an investment-grade business, not because Spirit Airlines or an emerging market airline has great credit themselves, but it's because of the shortage of commercial aviation in the world. en_summary: UBS models $META Muse at 3M daily users, requiring ~3,000 $AMD EPYC chips in base case (750K agents with 4x CPU sharing) or ~23,800 without sharing. At 100M users, nearly 100,000 chips plus 8GB RAM and 100GB SSD per agent, pushing DRAM toward 2TB per host, creating opportunity for $MU and $SNDK.
text:
UBS models $META Muse at just 3M daily users with number of $AMD EPYC chips required depending heavily on how many agents are running simultaneously and how efficiently CPU capacity is shared: 

• Base case ~3,000 chips if 750K agents run simultaneously with 4x CPU sharing
• High engagement ~23,800 chips if 1.5M agents run simultaneously without CPU sharing

But the bigger opportunity is what happens as adoption scales because same base assumptions would imply nearly 100,000 EPYC chips at 100M daily users while each Muse agent also requires its own 8GB of RAM and 100GB of SSD storage.

That could push DRAM requirements toward 2TB per host at 4x CPU sharing creating a huge opportunity for $MU and $SKHY in DRAM and $SNDK in NAND flash storage.

*  Society is ill prepared for the negative consequences and safety issues associated with AI.

*  The AI creators and practitioners take no responsibility for those consequences and issues.  Indeed, they are trying to the opposite - evading accountability.

text:
I think Satoshi’s Bitcoin should be left alone.

I get the concern about quantum attacks. But we keep talking about permissionless money and getting rid of middlemen, yet we’re debating whether someone should be allowed to spend their own Bitcoin.

How does that make sense?

Whether Satoshi is alive or dead, those coins aren’t ours to control. Just because someone disappears doesn’t mean we get to make that decision for them. Even if the network agrees to freeze those coins, I still have a problem with it.

If we’re comfortable changing the rules to lock Satoshi out of their own Bitcoin, what makes you think we won’t eventually find an excuse to do it to someone else?

en_summary: AI selloff is about cash flow, financing cost and waiting for returns, not demand evaporating. Demand remains strong: SK hynix Q3 revenue 104.6T won (+328% YoY), OP 83.3T with ~80% margin, DRAM/HBM sold out through 2029. Anthropic unit economics improving sharply, first quarterly OP. Hyperscalers Amazon, Alphabet, Meta maintain or raise 2026 capex, still leaving demand unmet. Market focuses on negative FCF and financing gap. NASDAQ trailing PE high-20s vs 190x in 2000.
text:
The AI selloff is not about demand evaporating. It is about cash flow, financing cost and how long the market is willing to wait for the returns.

Demand signals remain extremely strong.

SK hynix just reported Q3 revenue of 104.6 trillion won (+328% YoY) and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won with an ~80% margin. Management said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively sold out through 2029, customer HBM requests are roughly double what they can supply, and they expect the supply shortage to persist through 2030. Long-term agreements already cover more than half of 2027–2028 capacity with 14 major customers. That is not a demand problem.⁠

Anthropic’s S-1 shows the unit economics at the model layer improving sharply. Revenue per dollar of compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026 - a 5.2× improvement in five quarters. Compute costs fell from 251% of revenue to 48%. The company generated its first quarterly operating profit. Revenue grew 1,368% YoY while compute expense rose only ~300%. Efficiency is rising, not collapsing.⁠

GPU rental prices have turned higher again. B200 on-demand rates rose more than 20% in a month in some indices; H100 and H200 also firmed. Tightness in the spot and short-term rental market is consistent with the hyperscalers’ own comments that they still cannot meet all the demand they see.⁠

On the supply side the hyperscalers themselves are not signalling a slowdown. Amazon maintained ~$220 billion 2026 cash cape

~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corporate bonds and loans mature over the next 5 years, including $438 billion due by the end of 2028.

The amount of junk-rated debt maturing within 2 years alone has surged +31% YoY.

At the same time, $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt is coming due by 2031.

The corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.

"CHAIRMAN WARSH: Thank you, Claire. Interest rates get in the cracks, interest rates affect directly or indirectly, almost everything. And what have we seen? Since early September what we've seen inside of the technology complex, outside of the technology complex, whether you pronounce it AI or SI, Claire, is up to you, what have you seen?

Interest rates have had an effect. You've seen market participants that are discriminating between the kinds of investments they want to make. You've seen credit spreads for certain assets widen out, gap out. For others you've seen some tightening in financial conditions, but not significantly.

I have somewhat different view than most having cut my options teeth on a dispersion book during the tech bubble.  

The index vol short half of the short correlation trade was always a choice in terms of its sizing.  Back then IV/RV premium was pretty narrow unlike today so every unit of Vega sold in index was managed carefully.  Being short index vol was a coin flip sort of trade.   The sizing ranged from Vega neutral to single stock book (which collected theta) to theta neutral which was Vega long. 

The drop in implied correlation makes the trade less attractive.  But given the level of implied on index the notable risk isn't selling index vol to low its buying single name vol way way too high.  The root causes of that single name vol levels are numerous including speculative demand and the dispersion trader competing to buy elevated single name vol.  the seller is absent and gets a sweet risk premium when providing any liquidity. So then it comes down to hedging index level and sizing.

en_summary: Ksidiii: Remember boiler room pump-and-dump schemes of the 2000s and garbage bonds in the 90s. People chuckle at who would fall for that. This is exactly what QIS is in today’s era. Banks charge a markup on absolute garbage strategies that never work, then rotate them in and out. Quoted on alpha decay of published strategies.
text:
Remember the boiler room pump-and-dump schemes of the 2000s, where brokers would sell garbage stocks at massive markups? The same thing happened with garbage bonds in the ’90s. A lot of folks today look back and chuckle, asking, “Who would be dumb enough to fall for that?” To them, these were clearly horrible investments and outright grifts.

This is exactly what QIS is in today’s era. Banks charge a markup on absolute garbage strategies that never work, then rotate them in and out every few months with a “new idea” after the old one breaks.

There are hundreds of billions of dollars in these horrible programs across almost every tier-one platform. It’s very sad to see pensions and other institutions blow capital on this type of stuff.
